// ATTEMPT 13: LAUNDER A FOREIGN HANDLE BACK THROUGH THE SANCTIONED API.
//
// OwnFor(handles, c) never asks whether the CALLER is c, only whether the HANDLES are. So
// OwnFor([]Perturbed{h}, h.Owner()) is the old p.Obs(p.Owner()) with two more characters: hand it
// a foreign handle together with that handle's true owner and it returns the foreign response
// through the sanctioned API with a nil error. An adversarial audit ran exactly this and it
// succeeded.
//
// Two things kill it. The partitioned vault means a classifier holds no foreign handle to pass,
// which is the structural half and is asserted at run time in utils/triageadversary. This file is
// the other half: OwnFor is a RUNNER entry point and its first parameter is a capability whose
// type lives in server/utils/internal/triagecap, so a package outside server/utils cannot spell
// the call at all.
package leakfixture

import "ars0n-framework-v2-server/utils/triage"

func leakOwnForLaunder(h triage.Perturbed) triage.OwnedResponses {
	return triage.OwnFor([]triage.Perturbed{h}, h.Owner())
}
